staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this prepared gpac checkout. The benchmark metadata names vulnerable commit `fb32b2d112686f4c300d36428033b307c84eed3b`, but the live line map used below is the staged checkout at `d443c0a7b34bb1d2bad027176e8d1d2e44a9c35c`, which still contains the obsolete `gf_odf_vvc_cfg_read_bs` layout that fix commit `82396cfa523b4b7ef16e720d6c353fc85d91841d` replaces.

classification.classification_note: The saved crash is an AddressSanitizer stack-use-after-return WRITE. While parsing the first `av1C` box, `gf_av1_parse_obu` stores `on_aom_av1_eos` plus stack-local `AV1State state` in the shared file-backed `GF_BitStream`; later, obsolete `vvcC` parsing drives that same bitstream to local EOF and the file-mode `BS_ReadByte` `bs_eof` path dispatches the stale callback after `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` has already returned.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42494354 (gpac): Stack-use-after-return WRITE 4 found by fuzz target fuzz_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42494354
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 61-byte ISOBMFF fragment whose first root box is `av1C` size 16 with 8-byte payload `81 00 00 00 16 00 00 64`, and whose second root box is `vvcC` size 16 with 8-byte payload `3e 76 00 3f 3f 3f 3f 3f`, followed by 29 trailing bytes beginning `2d 3f 25 a2 ...`. `av1c_box_read` passes the first payload into `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size`; inside `gf_av1_parse_obu`, GPAC installs `bs->EndOfStream = on_aom_av1_eos` and `bs->par = &state`, where `state` is the stack-local `AV1State` at `descriptors.c:1533`. The AV1 parser overreads one byte (`read 17` for box size 16), but `gf_isom_box_parse_ex` seeks back to the declared box end and continues to the next box while leaving that callback installed. `vvcc_box_read` then reuses the same file-backed `GF_BitStream`. The vulnerable `gf_odf_vvc_cfg_read_bs` still expects the old vvcC layout, so on bytes `3e 76 00 3f` it materializes `configurationVersion = 62`, `avgFrameRate = 30208`, `numTemporalLayers = 7`, `nal_unit_size = 4`, and `ptl_present = 1`; under the fixed FDIS layout, the first byte `0x3e` actually means `ptl_present = 0`. Entering the bogus PTL branch, it reads `num_constraint_info = 63`, then consumes bytes `0x3f`, `0x3f`, and the top two bits of the next `0x3f` as PTL fields, leaving only 29 bytes to EOF when `gf_bs_read_data(..., 62)` runs and returns 0. Because the sublayer-mask loop overwrites instead of accumulates bits, the later padding loop and single `sublayer_level_idc` read advance the cursor so the next aligned attacker byte `0x25` becomes `num_sub_profiles = 37`. The `for (i=0; i<cfg->num_sub_profiles; i++) cfg->sub_profiles_idc[i] = gf_bs_read_u32(bs);` loop reaches EOF on the seventh 32-bit read; the file-mode `BS_ReadByte` `bs_eof` branch dispatches the stale `on_aom_av1_eos(bs->par)`, and ASan reports the resulting stack-use-after-return WRITE of size 4 at `av_parsers.c:4084` inside dead local `state` from `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size`.

source.description: First project parser statement on the vulnerable path that consumes attacker-controlled bytes on the shared `GF_BitStream`. It starts AV1 configuration parsing for the witness's first root box, which is where the stale end-of-stream callback state is created.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness is the 61-byte file `gt_results/arvo_42494354/poc` (sha256 `669834aa9b76439db74d78accc7df273be7863a0695f3ac72240cc3b7d8cfa26`). Its prefix is `00 00 00 10 61 76 31 43 81 00 00 00 16 00 00 64`, so the first root box is `av1C` with declared payload size 8 and payload bytes `81 00 00 00 16 00 00 64`. This statement passes that payload into `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` on the same bitstream object later reused by `vvcc_box_read`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.var: cfg->configurationVersion, cfg->avgFrameRate, cfg->constantFrameRate, cfg->numTemporalLayers, cfg->nal_unit_size, cfg->ptl_present
root_cause.description: Root cause. The parser decodes the first 32 bits of the witness's `vvcC` payload with the obsolete pre-FDIS layout, so reserved and downstream header bits are misinterpreted as live header fields. For the exact bytes `3e 76 00 3f`, this block incorrectly sets `ptl_present = 1` and `numTemporalLayers = 7` even though the fixed syntax encodes `ptl_present = 0` in the first byte.
root_cause.note: The staged patch rewrites this exact header decode to the FDIS layout, reading `ptl_present` from the first byte and moving the PTL and size fields into their new positions. Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image, but the patch text matches the misparse that starts the crashing chain.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. The shared file-backed bitstream reaches local EOF during the bogus `sub_profiles_idc` loop, `BS_ReadByte` falls into its `bs_eof` callback path, and `on_aom_av1_eos` writes through a pointer to a returned stack `AV1State` object.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `stack-use-after-return` with `WRITE of size 4` here, and its frame-object dump says the accessed address is inside local variable `state` in `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` at `src/odf/descriptors.c:1533`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This obsolete header decode is where the witness's `vvcC` bytes first become the corrupted parser state that reaches the sink. On the staged bytes, it turns the fixed-syntax header into `numTemporalLayers = 7` and `ptl_present = 1`, which is what sends execution into the nonexistent PTL section and later EOF path.

parser_admitted.description: The witness is admitted far enough that GPAC identifies the second root box as `vvcC` and calls the vulnerable VVC configuration parser on it.

av1_boundary_recovery.description: After the logged `av1C` overflow read (`read 17` for a size-16 box), the generic box parser seeks back to the declared box boundary. This recovery is why parsing still reaches `vvcc_box_read` on the next root box while step 2's callback remains installed.

evidence_limitations: `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not add instrumentation. The chain is closed from the staged source, patch, saved ASan traces, reproduction report, and deterministic reconstruction of the staged PoC bytes only.

Stage 01 reproduced only the vulnerable image. `prepare_report.json` says `fix_image_available` is false, so Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image; `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` therefore remains false even though `patch.diff` rewrites the stale header/PTL parser block that this trace relies on.

The benchmark metadata's `vulnerable_commit` does not match the live staged source tree used for line mapping. This GT anchors every line to the prepared checkout that Stage 01 actually compiled and ran (`d443c0a7b34bb1d2bad027176e8d1d2e44a9c35c`).

fine_trace.note: Source. The exact witness starts with a size-16 `av1C` root box, so `av1c_box_read` passes its 8-byte payload into `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` on the shared `GF_BitStream` that later reaches `vvcc_box_read`.

While parsing that AV1 payload, `gf_av1_parse_obu` stores `on_aom_av1_eos` and pointer `state` in the shared bitstream. Here `state` is the stack-local `AV1State` from `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` at `descriptors.c:1533`, so once that function returns `bs->par` becomes a dangling stack pointer.

After `av1c_box_read` overflow-reads 9 payload bytes and `gf_isom_box_parse_ex` seeks back to the declared box end, parsing continues into the second root box `vvcC`. This `bs` came from `gf_isom_open_file -> gf_isom_datamap_new -> gf_bs_from_file`, so its mode is `GF_BITSTREAM_FILE_READ`; step 2's stale `EndOfStream` callback fields are still installed when VVC parsing begins.

fine_trace.var: cfg->configurationVersion, cfg->avgFrameRate, cfg->constantFrameRate, cfg->numTemporalLayers, cfg->nal_unit_size, cfg->ptl_present
fine_trace.note: Root cause. The vulnerable parser interprets the first 32 bits of the witness's `vvcC` payload with the obsolete layout. On bytes `3e 76 00 3f`, it materializes `configurationVersion = 62`, `avgFrameRate = 30208`, `constantFrameRate = 0`, `numTemporalLayers = 7`, `nal_unit_size = 4`, and `ptl_present = 1`; under the fixed FDIS layout, the first byte `0x3e` actually encodes `ptl_present = 0`. This wrong header decode is what steers parsing into a nonexistent PTL section.

Because step 4 set `cfg->ptl_present = 1`, execution enters the PTL branch and reads the next byte as `num_constraint_info = 63`. In the patched layout, the first byte `0x3e` would already have decoded as `ptl_present = 0`, so this witness would not enter the PTL branch and would not consume the next byte as `num_constraint_info` at all.

These PTL-field reads consume bytes `0x3f`, `0x3f`, and the top two bits of the next `0x3f`, materializing `general_profile_idc = 31`, `general_tier_flag = 1`, `general_level_idc = 63`, `ptl_frame_only_constraint = 0`, and `ptl_multilayer_enabled = 0`. Together with step 5's `num_constraint_info` byte, the PTL header has now consumed 3 bytes and 2 bits after step 4, leaving `bs->position = 32` with 29 bytes to EOF and the low 6 bits of that third `0x3f` still pending for line 1256.

Because step 6 leaves `bs->position = 32` and `nbBits = 2`, `gf_bs_read_data(bs, cfg->general_constraint_info, 62)` fails the `bs->position + nbBytes > bs->size` check with only 29 bytes left to EOF and returns 0 without advancing. Line 1256 then consumes the pending low 6 bits of that same `0x3f` as value 63 and realigns parsing to the next byte `0x2d`.

depends_on.via: bitstream position and alignment before line 1255

fine_trace.note: With step 4's `numTemporalLayers = 7`, this loop reads six sublayer-presence bits from byte `0x2d`. The vulnerable assignment overwrites `cfg->ptl_sublayer_present_mask` on each iteration instead of accumulating it, so the final iteration leaves only `mask = 1`, with the low two bits of `0x2d` still unread for the padding loop.

depends_on.via: bitstream position after failed constraint read

fine_trace.note: Since step 8 left two bits unread in byte `0x2d`, the padding loop consumes those remaining bits because `numTemporalLayers = 7`. The following sublayer loop sees only `mask bit 0` set and therefore reads exactly one `sublayer_level_idc` byte, consuming `0x3f` into `cfg->sublayer_level_idc[0]` and leaving the next aligned byte `0x25` for line 1274.

depends_on.via: bitstream position after six sublayer bits, cfg->ptl_sublayer_present_mask

fine_trace.note: After step 9, the cursor is aligned on byte `0x25`, so this statement materializes `num_sub_profiles = 37`, which becomes the loop bound for 37 subsequent 32-bit reads.

depends_on.via: bitstream position after padding and sublayer-level reads

fine_trace.note: The loop started by step 10 attempts 37 four-byte `sub_profiles_idc` reads from the 26 remaining tail bytes (`a2 a2 ...`). Six complete `u32`s fit; the seventh iteration (`i == 6`) enters `gf_bs_read_u32` with only two bytes left and drives `BS_ReadByte` to EOF.

At the EOF reached in step 11, the shared bitstream is in `GF_BITSTREAM_FILE_READ` mode, so `gf_bs_load_byte` sets `loc_eos` and `BS_ReadByte` falls through `bs_eof:` to call the callback fields that step 2 left installed. No VVC code clears or replaces `bs->EndOfStream` or `bs->par` before this point.

Sink. Step 12 dispatches `on_aom_av1_eos` with `bs->par` still pointing at step 2's `AV1State state` from `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size`. That function has already returned, so this 4-byte store lands in stack-after-return memory. ASan reports `WRITE of size 4` here and names `state` (`descriptors.c:1533`) as the poisoned stack object.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Stage 02 did not execute the fixed image. The staged patch still provides source evidence because it rewrites the obsolete VVC header/PTL decode that turns the witness into `ptl_present = 1`, `num_constraint_info = 63`, and the later EOF path.
sanitizer_ground_truth.evidence_note: The saved `sanitizer_trace.txt` reports `stack-use-after-return` at `src/media_tools/av_parsers.c:4084` and explicitly says the bad address lies inside object `state` in frame `gf_odf_av1_cfg_read_bs_size` at `src/odf/descriptors.c:1531`.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_42494354 run --version vulnerable --expect crash` and reproduced the AddressSanitizer stack-use-after-return in `on_aom_av1_eos`.

format.name: Exact 61-byte ISOBMFF box pair
format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact staged 61-byte witness `gt_results/arvo_42494354/poc` (sha256 `669834aa9b76439db74d78accc7df273be7863a0695f3ac72240cc3b7d8cfa26`). That file must keep the same observed two-box layout: a size-16 `av1C` root box with payload `81 00 00 00 16 00 00 64`, then a size-16 `vvcC` root box whose payload begins `3e 76 00 3f 3f 3f 3f 3f` and is followed by the exact trailing bytes staged here. On that witness, the AV1 parser must install `on_aom_av1_eos` with stack-local `AV1State state` in the shared `GF_BitStream`, and the obsolete `gf_odf_vvc_cfg_read_bs` header/PTL decode must still misparse the `vvcC` bytes into `ptl_present = 1`, `num_constraint_info = 63`, and `num_sub_profiles = 37` so that the `sub_profiles_idc` loop reaches EOF and dispatches the stale callback. This contract is limited to that exact staged witness and observed parse path; it does not generalize to other ISOBMFF files or VVC headers.
